summary:
I wrote plan.md: one straight granite church on the summit along z 64. It has a 4-bay Romanesque nave (x 15..47, ridge y 73), a 15-block crossing tower with its parapet at y 100, and an octagonal deepslate spire with crockets up to y 142. A gold St Michael with a lightning-rod sword ends at exactly y 151. The Flamboyant choir and apse (x 63..97, ridge 86) have flying buttresses, pinnacles and a ring of chapels, standing on the crypt. The Merveille (x 56..107) is a 3-storey buttressed wall rising from y 6 on the north, with the cloister on top. Stepped south ranges with chimneys, the Grand Degré stair, and the Châtelet and Belle Chaise at the east complete it. I checked the footprint and heights by script, but nothing is built or rendered yet. The real church bends about 15°; I kept it straight so its roofs read clean. Two of my block ids were also flagged: the checker didn't know `chain`, so the plan uses no chains at all. Granite abbey on the rock: church on z64 with crossing tower, dark octagonal spire and gold St Michael (top y151), Flamboyant choir with flyers, Merveille north wall with cloister, logis south, Châtelet east.
Six trade-split parts: shell, slate roofs, spire/angel, choir, fittings, chimneys/lights/grounds. elements.md lists 17 elements; plan.md has palette, vocabulary, parts.

Rock and granite shell: parts/shell.mjs builds the rock-founded granite shell for all masses: nave, aisles, transepts, crossing tower with parapet, west front and terrace, Merveille with buttresses, logis, Degré with bridge, Châtelet with vault and turrets, and the ranges and gables. Openings are left as air for later parts. make.sh runs clean, with 0 refused writes and no floating blocks.
The choir is only a solid crypt to y43; P4 builds its walls above.
polish: Choir, ambulatory and chapel walls above y43 are P4's.
I did not check the palette line or run `mcd fit`.
Window stairs heads, sills and glass are P5's (the holes are air).
No lantern posts or parapet connections: parapet walls are plain posts without connection states.
Gable ends are written in the shell for most ranges, which may overlap what P2's roof tool expects.
Cloister stylobate ring and garth at y40 are left empty for P5.
Interiors above the floor courses are hollow shells; the ranges and sealed tower are open to the sky until P2 roofs them.

waste.what: Built a generic mass/hole/gable/crown helper set locally. Wrote the window and opening coordinates by hand from the plan's lists.
waste.cost: about 40 minutes of design and one large file; no retries
waste.tool: A vocab helper `shell_mass(footprint-fn, top, floor)` that does ground-founded perimeter walls plus fill. Also `gable(axis, c, lo, hi, y0, y1)` and `opening(box)` that registers cells as reserved air.

waste.what: Checked the result only by eye from two iso tiles.
waste.cost: 2 renders
waste.tool: A `mcd check` mode that lists wall columns not reaching the ground map, and masses whose roof/gable is missing.

companions.task: Quoins, string courses and arch heads per facade, plus the window surrounds.
Verify ground maps against walls, and the Degré and Châtelet stair levels.
Gable pitch and eave overhangs matching the gable walls.

summary:
Slate roofs: parts/roofs.mjs builds the slate roofs per ROOFS: 14 gables (nave, transepts, choir, Merveille E, N-CH, NW-R/NW-W, Belle Chaise, Châtelet, E-R, SE-R, LOGIS-W/A/B/C, BAILLI, SW-P), nave aisle lean-tos, the cloister ring roof, 9 chapel caps, NE turret cone and SW-T pyramid (23,429 blocks, no refusals, no off-palette).
make.sh completes with a whole build.nbt; render shows the roof masses at their plan heights, though gable ends read as flat dark slabs (solid fill prism).
Floating cells remain only where the owning part hasn't built support yet: cloister ring (shell has no cloister walls at y45..49) and chapel caps (chapel walls from P4).
polish: No roof.json and no `$MCD roof --spec` / trusses pass: all roofs are hand-placed with slate_stair_roof and lean/cloister loops, so there are no fascia, verge boards, ridge caps, overhangs or trusses, and the trusses/dormer requirements of the roofer card are unmet.

Gable ends are solid cobbled_deepslate prisms (slate_stair_roof fills under the stairs across the whole triangle), so from the front the transept and nave gables read as flat dark slabs; a real gable wall (masonry/timber) from the shell is needed in those triangles.

Cloister ring roof (x62..78, z13..27; d0 at y50, d1 at y46) floats: shell has no cloister outer wall at y45..49, and P5 must supply the lintel/columns at y41..45. Garth overhang (1 cell at y46) not built.
Chapel caps CH-N (79,47),(86,47), CH-S (68,75,82,89 at z80), CH-E (98 at z57,64,71) at y58..61 float until P4 builds the chapel walls to y57.

Not built: MERV-S lean-to (x85..101 z28..38, y46..51), NW-S stepped range, LOGIS dormers (x 24,32,40 / 61,67 / 76,82 / z92,98), CHAT-T turret caps, choir apse half-cone/hip to (89,86,64), NE-R walk roof, SW-T uses a 3-wide pyramid approximation, NE-T cone is a 3x3 approximation.
Pitches are chosen so each ridge hits its plan course exactly, so a few pitches are steeper than the 3:2 the plan names (N-CH is 7:3, choir 13:6).

waste.what: Pitch and eave/ridge arithmetic per roof, worked out by hand (pitch = [ridge-eave, half-span] so the ridge lands on the plan height).
waste.cost: about 25 gable calls worked out one by one; several retries when the helper's `height` argument turned out relative, not absolute
waste.tool: A roof helper that takes [x0,eave,z0,x1,ridge,z1,axis] and derives the pitch itself, plus `$MCD roof --spec` on a roof.json from the ROOFS table.

waste.what: A footprint and y<=151 gate wrapper around the grid, written by hand because vocab helpers write only into air inside their box and never check the footprint.
waste.cost: one wrapper, two extra fixes (missing inBounds, a y-range check on chapel_cap)
waste.tool: A build-library `guardFootprint(g, onFootprint)` (or vocab helpers that clip to the footprint) so every part gets footprint clipping for free.

waste.what: Lean-to slopes and the cloister ring written cell by cell with per-cell stair facings.
waste.cost: about 1,000 block-level writes in loops; facings worked out by hand
waste.tool: A `leanTo(g, rect, lowY, highY, highSide)` brush and a `ringRoof(g, outerRect, innerRect, ...)` brush in the build library.

waste.what: Verifying floating roof cells by reading block ids at single coordinates.
waste.cost: about 10 blockAt probes across two passes
waste.tool: `$MCD check` lists floating groups already; a `--explain` that names the missing support course would have saved the probes.

waste.what: Checking the roof reads by eye from the render sheet only.
waste.cost: one sheet render, eyeballed; no per-roof measurement
waste.tool: `$MCD roof --detect` or a per-roof ridge-height report from the grid would confirm the plan heights without eyeballing.

companions.task: Trusses, purlins and ridge beams for the nave, transepts and Merveille, and the rafter sets for the aisle lean-tos and dormers (the trusses block of roof.json).
The cloister ring: the outer wall to y49 and the arcade lintel y45, so the cloister roof sits on real supports.
The Degré and the Châtelet internal stair, so the Châtelet's roof has a stair to a real loft.
Gable-end verge boards, fascia and ridge caps, and the hip mitres on the choir apse and cloister corners.

summary:
Spire and archangel: Spire and archangel built in parts/spire.mjs: corner pinnacles y101..112, hollow r4 lantern stage y99..107 with glazed lancets and a cap y108, solid r3/r2/r1 needle to y137 with ribs and crockets, 1x1 column to y142.
Archangel on a pedestal at y143 with the sword tip at y151, the build's highest block.
make.sh saves a whole build.nbt: 1008 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette; check shows no floating groups, fit OK.
polish: The lancets are plain gray glass panes, not tracery; the glazier could replace them with a proper lancet head.
The 8 crockets and their 27 orphan flags in `mcd check` are expected by design (they stand off the spire face), not defects.

waste.what: Spire built as per-course octagon loops with hand-written inside/edge/vertex tests, because octagon_ring draws outlines only and I needed fills, ribs and lancet skips.
waste.cost: about 4 retries of the course function and a few minutes of coordinate reasoning
waste.tool: A build-library octagon helper with fill, ribs (vertex cells), a skip predicate for openings, and a per-course tapering spec (radius and y range per stage).

waste.what: Checked the crown and shaft footprint by reading shell.mjs to find which corner cells the balustrade occupies, to place the pinnacles.
waste.cost: one grep and one sed read
waste.tool: A reserved-cells or occupancy query for an earlier part's cells (e.g. the `mcd plan` view) that prints which cells are taken before a part starts.

waste.what: Verified the archangel and spire by zooming at several points, one zoom call at a time.
waste.cost: 3 zoom renders
waste.tool: A single render call that frames a named bounding box (e.g. `mcd zoom --box`) so one part can be checked in one step.

companions.task: Lay the octagonal courses of the spire and the ribs at the vertices, checking the taper by eye against the concept art.
Glaze the eight lantern lancets with proper tracery panes instead of plain gray glass panes.
Light the lantern stage and the hanging lamp so the gilded archangel catches the dusk light, and check the balustrade lamp spots.

summary:
Flamboyant choir: parts/choir.mjs builds the Flamboyant choir: solid granite walls z57/z71 and the east end and apse outline (x63..96, y43..72), clerestory tracery in two tiers per bay, balustrade y73 with pier pinnacles, north and south flying buttresses, chapel walls and caps, and chapel lancets.
make.sh saves a whole build.nbt; the choir line shows 6079 placed, no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE, and `check` reports 0 floating blocks with `fit` OK.
The east and south zooms show the bays, pinnacles, apse window and chapel caps; the glass reads dark, and the north flyers and the apse window were not checked close-up.
polish: Triforium glazing y59..61 not built; chapel corner pinnacles to y63 not built; apse diagonal flyers and the second lower south flyer not built.
Culée shafts have no crockets (plan wanted stair crockets at y73 and y75); tip is a polished_andesite_slab at y79.
South culées at z78..80 overlap CH-S boxes at x66..70 and x87..91; the chapel fill skips occupied cells, so the join is only partly verified.
Chapel caps are r=1 rings over 5-wide chapels, so they read as small squat pyramids rather than the plan's proper chapel caps.
Tracery glass reads as dark recesses in the zoom; check the glass and mullion material against the concept once the glazing pass is in.
Choir wall top y72 and the roof's eave at y73 meet the parapet line only if roofs.mjs keeps z58/z70 clear; the roof part has not been checked against this.

waste.what: Worked out the choir wall and chapel box coordinates by hand, and probed single cells (g.blockAt) to find which walls the shell had left open.
waste.cost: about 6 probe and edit cycles; the shell's 'walls above are P4' note was only found by reading the shell source
waste.tool: A shell-to-part handover list in plan.md (per mass: which y bands and walls the shell leaves open for a later part), so P4 knows the walls are its own without reading shell.mjs.

waste.what: Chapel_cap height is relative to y, not an absolute top, so my first pass built finials to y119. I caught it only in the structure check.
waste.cost: one full rebuild and a 'check' pass
waste.tool: Make chapel_cap's height argument absolute (or name it 'rise'), and state the convention in the vocab comment.

waste.what: Didn't know whether tracery_window's columns run along x or z on an east face, so I placed the apse window by guess.
waste.cost: one render to see the apse; the window is probably right but unverified
waste.tool: A face-aware wall-run helper (wallRun(face, a, b)) that maps a face and horizontal span to cells, shared by tracery, lancet and parapet.

waste.what: Drew the apse outline with a hand-written rounding line walker (wallLine) because the vocab has no polyline wall helper.
waste.cost: about 15 minutes of coordinate reasoning in total
waste.tool: A polyline or polygon wall brush in build.mjs (wallPolyline(g, points, y0, y1, material), air-only).

waste.what: Solid chapel fill is a box loop over air-only writes, repeated per chapel.
waste.cost: one loop, but it has to run after the lancets or it fills their cells
waste.tool: A box fillAir(g, box, material) brush that skips occupied cells, so the order against lancets stops mattering.

companions.task: Build the choir walls, piers, apse outline and flying-buttress culées and their pinnacle shafts (the solid granite and stone-brick crockets), and check the arc springing at the culée inner face.
Set the clerestory and apse glass: fit the mullions and ogee heads so the panes show light, and check the triforium glazing that was not built.
Light the choir balustrade, pinnacles and chapel caps so no walkable surface spawns mobs at dusk, once the lantern pass lands.

summary:
Windows, doors, cloister: parts/fittings.mjs builds the openings the shell left as air: nave aisle tracery windows and clerestory lancets, west door and window, south transept and logis terrace doors, Merveille lancets, logis mullion windows, Belle Chaise lancets, turret slits.
It also builds the cloister: stylobate ring y40, staggered quartz colonnade, grass garth at y40 (1244 blocks, 0 refused, 0 off-palette).
make.sh produces a whole build.nbt; fit is OK and check shows 0 floating/unsupported. Machicolations, the Châtelet entry and the Belle Chaise door are not built.
polish: Machicolation corbels on the Châtelet (y 30..31, all round) not built; the entry arch is the shell's.
Belle Chaise door from the Châtelet (116, 27..30, 52..53) not built.
Pane connection states are set to all-true in my rectangle glazing helper (glazeRect), not checked in a close-up render; the vocab helpers' own connections are used elsewhere.
Cloister lean-to slate roof belongs to P2; dormers and chimneys to P2/P6.
Render checked only at whole-abbey scale (front elevation shows the Merveille lancets as dark slits) and one cloister zoom; the nave and logis windows were not close-up checked.
The clerestory openings are three lancets per 3-wide bay (1 cell of glass each), not the plan's 3-wide arched tracery; the head row sits in the hole's top cell, so they read as narrow slits.

waste.what: Glazed rectangles (west-front window, transept and logis door surrounds, cloister garth) were drawn cell by cell with a local glazeRect loop and a local put() air-check.
waste.cost: about 40 lines of loops; a few dozen g.set calls
waste.tool: A build-library glazing-rectangle helper (air-only, mullion every third column, pane connections set for the wall plane) in vocab/h3 or the build library would have replaced glazeRect.

waste.what: Found that colonnade_bay and the other vocab helpers skip non-air cells silently: the report said 0 refused while the cloister's stylobate and garth were partly blocked. I had to probe grid cells with g.get to confirm.
waste.cost: one probe script, about 3 tool calls
waste.tool: runParts or the helpers should report skipped cells (not only refused writes), so a helper that writes only into air counts its skips in the part report.

waste.what: Each shell opening (hole) had to be read from shell.mjs source by grep to match it with a helper of the right size; the holes list is not exported.
waste.cost: one grep and a sed read of about 30 lines
waste.tool: The shell part should export its openings as data (a list of {box, face, kind}) so the fittings part can iterate over them instead of re-deriving the sizes.

waste.what: Viewing a render: the full-abbey render is far too small to judge windows, so the close-up needed a separate zoom call per area.
waste.cost: 3 render or zoom calls, one image read each
waste.tool: mcd render with --closeups on the named openings (the Merveille lancets, the cloister arcades) in one pass.

companions.task: Check and set the pane connection states and the clerestory tracery: the nave clerestory lancets are 1 cell of glass each, where the plan wants a 3-wide arched tracery window.
Hang the doors (west, transept, logis terrace) with correct hinges and facings and check the door surrounds and the threshold steps.
Build the Châtelet machicolation corbels and the Belle Chaise door surround, which I did not reach in this session.

summary:
Chimneys, lights, grounds: parts/grounds.mjs builds all 8 RESERVED chimney stacks (3x3 masonry, centre flue, campfire at the foot, slab cap) and the lantern posts on the terraces, N-TER edge, Degré walls and SAUT-G corners.
make.sh runs whole: the grounds line shows 619 placed, no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE writes, and every stack seated.
Not done: paving/gravel, the chimney-fire fit issue at the stack caps, and the roofs, which are still skipped so the flue can't be checked through a real roof.
polish: Chimney fire fit (8 issues): fit reports the flue walled at the cap (stone_brick_slab ring at each stack's top y); the roof part is not yet built, so the roof-through-flue check cannot be verified. Re-check after parts/roofs.mjs lands and adjust the cap or let the roof stop against the stack.
Paving: no gravel or stone paving was laid on the courts and terraces (the GROUND map's bare rock between buildings); left to the shell or a later pass.
Lamps on the Degré walls: the coping slabs make bottom-slab supports, so those lanterns are skipped (about 4 of the 12 planned); the plan's wall lanterns need a full-block or top-slab support there.

plan.md checklist and elements.md ticks not edited: plan.md has no per-part checklist and my Read gate was not triggered for it; elements.md rows 14 (chimneys) and 17 (lighting) are built except the cap issue above.

waste.what: Chimney stacks written block by block with my own 3x3 flue loop, after chimney_stack's 2x2 ring left the flue open on the sides
waste.cost: two rebuilds and one redesign of the stack; about 8 seat searches by hand
waste.tool: a build-library chimney_stack option for a 3x3 masonry ring with a 1x1 air flue and a slab cap, so the fit check passes without a custom loop

waste.what: Lamp supports checked by reading the block below each candidate (slab or full block) and rerunning fit to find the bottom-slab lanterns
waste.cost: one failed fit run and one rebuild
waste.tool: lamp() with a support check that rejects bottom slabs, or a helper that places a lantern on a top slab or hangs it under a coping

waste.what: Chimney placement scanned by hand: the first air-over-solid cell per stack column, found by a debug column dump
waste.cost: a debug script and three column reads
waste.tool: a seat(g, x, z, cells) helper in the build library that returns the base y of a footprint of air cells over solid

companions.task: lay the terrace and court paving (stone, gravel, cobble on the bare rock) that the GROUND map leaves open, so I would not have to leave it to the shell
make the Degré coping lanterns and the slab-topped wall runs take a proper top-slab or full-block support, so the lamps on the stair walls land

summary: inspection: Walk passes (72 cells reached, no room unreachable). Fit went from 8 chimney-fire issues to OK after carrying each stack's stone-brick masonry through the roof line to the open top, with no slab cap, and keeping the roof out of the stack columns.
polish: The stacks' roof around the 3x3 columns is now simply open to the masonry (roof writes are refused in those columns); a roofer would cut the courses to meet the stack, which I did not check visually.
Campfire bases for the eight stacks moved (for example LOGIS-W 25,56,92 and 80,47,104), because the roof no longer fills the columns; I did not verify these sit on solid footing in rooms.
Stack caps are now plain stone_bricks with no slab cap; the plan's 'cap a ring of slabs' was dropped to satisfy the fit check.

waste.what: Working out which part put the blocking slab at each stack's cap level: the runParts report shows 0 refusals for the grounds part, so the cap writes were silently skipped (set only writes into air) and I had to infer the occupant by reading shell, roofs and the stack code.
waste.cost: about 6 tool calls and 3 rebuilds
waste.tool: The stack/cap writers should report when a write is skipped because a cell is occupied (or the fit message should name the occupying part and cell), so the offender is named directly.

waste.what: The fit message says 'the roof's stone_brick_slab' for any slab beside the flue at its top level, including my own cap slab once I moved the cap; the wording pointed at the roof when the rule is really 'no slab may wall the flue'.
waste.cost: 2 rebuild-and-check cycles
waste.tool: fit should name the block's owning part and say that a slab next to a flue counts as roof, so a cap is not mistaken for roof.

companions.task: Lay the chimney stacks: masonry through the roof line to the open top, flue open, chimney fire at the foot, so the stack reads as built stone rather than a slab-capped column.
Frame the roof around the stack columns (cut the courses to meet the masonry) so the slope stops cleanly against each chimney.
